The string-format bypass is implemented once in the shared bounded validator (`crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1211`) gated on `Mode::is_response()`, so it reaches every SDK root including non-Red-Team ones, while `Mode::Request` is untouched; min/max metadata is still parsed and fails closed even when the constraint is skipped (proved by `validation/tests.rs:568,586`). Operation selection uses an explicit generated `ZodResponseCompatibility` node with distinct `request`/`response` children (`validation.rs:542-555`, emitted at `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:337`); array and opaque baselines are explicitly classified and generation fails closed on ambiguous mappings, unclassified expressions, missing pairs or coverage drift (`red_team_dataplane.py:256-341`, guarded by seven negative tests in `tools/test_g25_generation.py`). Typed projection preservation is generated correctly: per-field decode with lossless fallback into existing extension storage, baseline-field decode failures still errors, no duplicate JSON keys, and baseline/extension collisions rejected (`tools/generate_models.py:482-506`, e.g. `models/generated.rs:8116`). Regression coverage is mechanically derived rather than hand-picked: 46 roots / 15,658 mutations with branch-valid witnesses and recorded null-branch skips (`tools/g25_fixtures.py`), checked against a genuinely independent oracle that imports the actual frozen Zod modules and AJV with network/env disabled, self-checks its adaptation semantics, asserts each pre-mutation witness is vendor-valid, and binds the corpus bytes by SHA-256 (`tools/g25-oracle.mts`); the Rust side re-verifies that digest (`tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:70`). All 55 projection fields are exercised for unset/conforming/null/wrong-type/nested and u128 values in both response modes, the three disputed strict cases stay rejected, job-1/p-1/map-1 and both reported timestamp forms pass through the real typed clients and transport, and the one decoder exemption (`set_runtime_profile`) is justified with a located witness and tested through the public client (`tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2518`). No blocker or high finding. The acceptance gap is narrower than the quality: `docs/VALIDATION.md:111` still tells readers the vendor response oracle retains "formats and bounds", which this phase made false (`tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs:19` now deletes `format`, `minLength`, `maxLength`), and the regex check skips its metadata validation in response modes where min/max do not. findings.description: The current validation reference states the 0.93.0 vendor response oracle "deliberately allows unknown response fields and string enum values while retaining types, requiredness, formats and bounds". This phase changed exactly that behavior: tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs:19 now deletes `format`, `minLength` and `maxLength` for the response policy, and crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1211 bypasses the eight format checks plus request-only string bounds in both response modes. The user-facing doc that describes the vendor response checks is therefore stale and contradicts docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md, and it carries no link to that report. docs/VALIDATION.md:13 also describes the response policy without mentioning format relaxation.
findings.required_fix: Update docs/VALIDATION.md (the "Current vendor response checks" paragraph and the response-policy paragraph at line 13) to state that string formats and vendor string length bounds are not retained under either response policy, that numeric/array bounds and types/requiredness are, and link docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md. Add a documentation guard (e.g. in tools/test_g25_report.py or tools/test_ci.py) that binds the documented response-policy wording to the keywords actually removed by tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs and tools/g25-oracle.mts, so the statement cannot drift again.

findings.description: In response modes the `regex` check is skipped by the `continue` before its metadata is read, so a malformed or unregistered pattern entry (missing `regex.$regexp`, or a source absent from `patterns()`) is silently accepted in Mode::Response / Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults while Mode::Request rejects it. min/max deliberately validate their `value` before the skip (lines 1199-1208) and `unit` is validated for every kind (lines 1193-1197), so this is the one asymmetric case. Generated graph metadata is currently guarded by tools/generate_models.py tests, so there is no demonstrated runtime defect; this is defense-in-depth only, and the maintainer recorded it as staged to phase 20.
findings.required_fix: Extract and validate the regex source (and its presence in the compiled pattern registry) before the response-mode skip, mirroring the min/max bound extraction, and extend crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/tests.rs:568 to cover malformed regex metadata in all three modes.

findings.description: Typed projection pairing selects the vendor counterpart by name heuristics - an alias table, the exact name, `name.removesuffix("Schema")`, and for unions the branch with the largest property-name overlap (line 418). Unlike response-floor selection, which the plan requires to be explicit and which fails closed, a wrong pair here would silently attach optional typed fields to a neighbouring model. Risk is contained because every addition is optional, the 55-row ledger is committed (contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json) with the count and request-only model set pinned in tools/test_g25_generation.py:295-305, and each field is proven to populate from a schema-derived witness in both modes, so a changed pairing fails the suite.
findings.required_fix: Record the resolved legacy-schema/vendor-schema pair for each of the 55 additions as an explicit committed mapping (or assert the heuristic result against one), and raise rather than silently skip when a root has no candidate, so future vendor renames cannot re-pair projections unnoticed.
